From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 09:27:10 -0700
Subject: Fwd: INC-20270308-5521 — observable spike, possible retry storm

FYI — forwarding traces from AtlasPay. Grafana shows a sharp jump in 5xx and connection timeouts on the serving fleet starting 08:49. Latency P95 climbs from 120ms -> 1.6s in 6 minutes. Error rate (5xx) moved from 0.4% -> 8% for their tenant.

Preliminary notes:
- Autoscaler didn't add capacity quickly for the hot partition (we observed backpressure on gRPC gateway).
- There is evidence of KV cache invalidation thrash for prefixes used heavily by AtlasPay (cache TTLs recently lowered in an optimization deploy).
- Client side retries (exponential backoff misconfigured by AtlasPay) look aggressive; combined with our downstream queueing it formed a retry amplification loop.

I am going to open a temporary tenant throttle and adjust prefix cache safety window. Dev — can you confirm if the recent config change to LRU window was deployed to prod at 08:45?

— Dylan
From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 09:34:51 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: INC-20270308-5521 — observables and quick mitigations

I rolled the LRU/TTL change at 08:41 in canary, and promoted to prod at 08:44 per the deploy log. The intention was to reduce memory pressure by shortening prefix cache TTL from 10m -> 1m; we underestimated hotspot behavior. The cache churn likely caused increased KV lookups to the storage layer, amplifying latencies under load.

Immediate actions I applied at 09:30:
- Reverted TTL to 10m for the prefix-cache policy (temp patch attached).
- Enabled a temp tenant-level token bucket for AtlasPay to cap request concurrency to 120 rps to prevent queue growth.
- Bumped the gateway connection pool limit for the affected pool by +20% and rotated a subset of frontdoor nodes to the new kernel with larger accept queue size.

I'm watching metrics now — error rate fell to 2.1% but still elevated. I recommend a short-term customer-friendly mitigation: 1) rollback of the canary LRU change for other tenants (done), 2) aggressive client-side retry guidance for AtlasPay (increase base backoff), 3) schedule cache warming run for their keyspace.

Attached: temp-rate-limit-policy.patch

- Error rate reduced from ~8% -> ~1.9% in ~30 minutes; still monitoring.

Subject: Post-incident summary: AtlasPay — root cause and next steps

Final summary for records and customer-facing postmortem:
Root cause:
- A cache TTL/LRU tuning change deployed at 08:44 reduced prefix-cache TTL from 10m -> 1m globally. This caused cache churn for AtlasPay's hot keyspace, creating sustained extra load to the KV storage layer. Combined with an aggressive client retry scheme and a slightly under-provisioned gateway pool for that partition, requests queued and produced elevated 5xx/429 and timeouts.

Why it amplified:
- Changes were rolled globally without per-tenant canary gating.
- Monitoring lacked per-tenant 5xx anomaly detection — we only noticed aggregate signals initially.
- Autoscaler policy had a cooldown tuned for smoothing, which delayed capacity addition for this sudden hotspot.

Permanent corrective actions (committed):
- Implement per-tenant canary gating for cache/TTL changes; default safe TTL and staged ramp (owner: dev_patel; ETA: 2027-03-10).
- Add per-tenant error-rate anomaly alerts and dashboard (owner: dylan_brooks; ETA: 2027-03-09).
- Adjust autoscaler fast-path for partition hot events: lower scale-in cooldown and introduce an emergency boost (owner: infra_team; ETA: 2027-03-15).
- Document explicit tenant throttling escape hatches and add to runbooks (owner: marissa_cole; ETA: 2027-03-09).
- Offer AtlasPay a 2-hour service credit and a technical review session (owner: aditya_rao; ETA: 2027-03-08 EOD).

Metrics at mitigation: 5xx dropped from 8% -> 1.1% within 45 minutes; latency P95 returned to 160ms from the 1.6s spike. No other tenants showed persistent impact.

Next steps: convert notes into full postmortem (will include detailed timeline, logs, and follow-up tickets). I'll schedule a cross-functional review tomorrow to validate fixes.

— Vivek
